perspective:
Alice Lim’s available information:

- She knows Austin as an old friend from high school; they are close and often discuss personal and professional lives. She knows her own career as a dental hygienist and understands Austin works in insurance.
- She observed Austin becoming reserved when work came up. She invited him for coffee because she suspected he might be hiding something about his job performance.
- She heard Austin say work was “nothing really,” just the “usual ups and downs,” and that he was “not sure how to handle a few things at work” and it was “complicated.”
- She believed Austin might be considering a career change because of dissatisfaction at work. She felt worried and chose to share her own healthcare experiences.
- She told Austin healthcare needs dedicated people and offered contacts. She heard Austin say he had thought about a change but didn’t know other paths, asked what she suggested, and said healthcare sounded interesting and he wanted to know more.
- She perceived Austin as hesitant due to fear of the unknown. She felt frustration and empathy.
- She told Austin about her friend Lara, who switched to healthcare in her late 30s and was happier. Austin said it was inspiring but he worried about risks and the initial struggle.
- She told Austin growth often comes from leaving comfort zones and that she would support him. Austin thanked her and said her support and real success stories helped.
- Seeing Austin’s openness, she felt encouraged and hopeful. She offered to connect him with a career counselor and friends in healthcare. Austin said that would be helpful and appreciated it.
- She said she would set up a meeting next week. Austin said he was looking forward to it.
- After discussions and meetings she participated in, she believed Austin was ready to take next steps and appreciated her help. She felt satisfaction and joy and planned regular check-ins.
- She heard Austin say he felt excited, a bit nervous, and mostly grateful. He agreed to regular check-ins to stay focused and valued her perspective.
